newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO PAY OFF DEBT TO POLAND.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO PAY OFF DEBT TO POLAND.

text.p: Romania will settle before mid-June a $5.5 million debt to Poland dating to the communist era, in line with a protocol signed in Bucharest earlier this year, a parliament's lower chamber statement showed on Tuesday.
It said the lower Chamber of Deputies had passed a bill on the protocol between the finance ministries of Romania and Poland on the settlement of the debt issue.
The protocol stipulates that ex-communist Romania should pay the outstanding debt in two installments before June 15.
"Poland was the last Comecon country to which we owed money," Finance Ministry manager Mihai Tanasescu said.
He said Romania had had communist-era debts to several countries members of the defunct Moscow-led Comecon trade alliance, but declined to elaborate on the size of those debts.
In its turn, Romania has to recover outstanding debts from several countries, including Cuba, Mongolia and North Korea, which also date to communist years, Tanasescu said, without giving details.
